title: Architecture Decision Record
description: Validates the structured front section of an ADR document. The narrative sections (Context, Options, Consequences) are prose; this schema constrains the fields a tool can index and check: identity, status, dates, links, and revisit triggers.

id.description: Sequential, zero-padded, never reused. Example: ADR-0007.

title.description: Imperative and specific, stating the choice: 'Use Postgres full-text search instead of a dedicated engine'. Not a noun like 'Search'.

status.description: Lifecycle state per the ADR reference. Accepted records are immutable; changes happen via new ADRs.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD, the date the decision was made (not backfilled unless stated in context).

deciders.description: Who decided. Names, roles, or team identifiers.

context.description: The forces in play: requirements, constraints, current state, and the scenario IDs (e.g. Q3) that put pressure on this decision.

options.description: At least two options, each steel-manned.

pros.description: Concrete benefits, tied to scenarios where possible.

cons.description: Concrete costs. An option with empty cons is advocacy, not analysis.

rejection_rationale.description: Required when chosen=false: the argument that actually killed the option, specific enough to re-run the decision if the cons stop applying.

decision.description: One imperative sentence: 'We will X.' If it cannot be one sentence, split the ADR.

harder.description: Every decision has a cost; an ADR listing none will be distrusted.

new_obligations.description: What must now be maintained, measured, or documented.

revisit_trigger.description: The observable, measurable condition under which this decision is re-examined, e.g. 'search p95 > 500 ms for two consecutive weeks'.

links.description: Decision-graph edges. An unlinked ADR is a disconnected monolith.

target.description: Another ADR id, or a repository document path.
